statements.quote: Look, our aspirations are to grow operating margin between 50 and 150 basis points every year through 2030. We certainly think that's feasible.

statements.quote: As we look in out years, I think there is still more, let us say, internal optimization to be done in terms of better matching supply and demand, ultimately yielding to 50 to 150 basis points of operating margin expansion on average for the next five years.

statements.doc_title: National Vision Holdings Inc Q2 2026 Earnings Call

street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (Visible Alpha). EBITDA margins in percent from the fundamentals 'EBITDA margin' row. Target-year comparison uses consensus adjusted operating income / revenue: FY2026 5.89%, FY2027 6.63%, FY2028 7.50%, FY2029 8.31%, FY2030 9.09% (FY2029 and FY2030 rows are thin, no broker margin row). Target 10.2% = fiscal 2025 adj operating margin 5.2% (Laden, Q4 2025 call, doc 198167) plus 5 years at the 100 bps midpoint; low end of range gives 7.7%, which consensus already exceeds. Gap at fiscal 2028 is 69.6 bps.

evidence_of_progress.note: Company-reported adjusted operating margin: Q1 fiscal 2026 +210 bps to 10.2% (doc 198166), Q2 fiscal 2026 +140 bps to 6.3% (doc 133219); H1 +180 bps; fiscal 2025 +160 bps to 5.2%. Full year AOI guide raised about 7.5% at Q2 (2026-08-12), partly a $5M tariff refund. Delivery so far is at or above the top of the 50 to 150 bps range, driven by SG&A leverage while traffic fell 4.9% in Q2.

verdict: Closest GXO analogue of the three: stock down 44% at the bottom of its 5-year EV/EBITDA range, a new CEO (hired from CooperVision as President in 2024, CEO since 2025-08-01) and new CFO who set and repeat a numeric 50 to 150 bps a year operating margin path through 2030, and consensus 2030 margin sits about 110 bps below the midpoint; caveats are that the street already sits above the low end, revisions are +8%, and the 2030 consensus is thin.
open_questions: Is the margin gain durable when Q2 traffic fell 4.9% and the expansion came from SG&A leverage, lower incentive comp and a marketing timing shift?
Does store growth re-acceleration to 60+ a year in 2028 dilute operating margin in the years the street models as the steepest step-up?
When exactly did Chris Laden start, and does the board refresh continue beyond the March 2025 additions?
